title: Q-Hitter: A Better Token Oracle for Efficient LLM Inference via Sparse-Quantized KV Cache
problem: LLM inference requires maintaining key-value caches that grow linearly with sequence length, consuming substantial GPU memory and limiting inference throughput. Existing KV cache management strategies fail to distinguish between critical and less important tokens.
motivation: Reducing KV cache memory footprint through selective token retention and quantization enables more efficient LLM inference and higher throughput deployment.
method: Q-Hitter employs a token oracle to predict which tokens are most important for attention computation. The system combines this token prediction with quantization to create a sparse-quantized KV cache that selectively retains high-importance tokens while quantizing embeddings to lower precision, reducing overall memory consumption.
key_novelty: Integration of a token oracle mechanism to guide sparse selection of KV cache entries paired with quantization for memory-efficient LLM inference.
contributions: Token oracle design for identifying critical tokens in KV cache
Sparse-quantized KV cache architecture combining sparsity and quantization
Demonstrated improvements in inference efficiency and memory utilization
primary_theme: KV cache compression via sparse quantization
